rules.pass_condition: All 3D (and well-formed 2D) 'all around' callouts include a valid Collection Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance/intersection indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A 3D 'all around' specification omits the Collection Plane indicator, or a 2D 'all around' specification relies on an ambiguous view without a Collection Plane.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 16 Collection Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator (or right of the Intersection Plane indicator for line profile).

rules.title: Prohibition of 'All Around' on Complex Workpieces With Ambiguous Closed Loops
rules.audit_check: The 'all around' indication SHALL NOT be used on complex workpieces where the collection plane intersects multiple disconnected closed loops (e.g., an outer perimeter plus an internal through-hole or cutout) and could cause ambiguity about which surfaces are included.
rules.pass_condition: 'All around' identifies one unmistakable continuous closed chain of features with no ambiguous internal/external loop conflict.
rules.fail_condition: 'All around' is applied to a part with internal holes or multiple cavities intersected by the same collection plane without disambiguation.
rules.remediation: Replace ambiguous 'all around' with explicit 'between' (A↔B), restricted-area demarcation (9.1.3), or separate individual feature specifications.

rules.title: Four Standardized Methods for Restricted Area Demarcation (ISO 128-24 Type 04.2 + TEDs)
rules.audit_check: When a geometrical tolerance applies only to a restricted portion of a feature, the restricted area SHALL be bounded using one of the 4 standardized Clause 9.1.3 methods: (1) long-dashed dotted wide line (ISO 128-24 type 04.2) + TEDs, (2) hatched area bounded by type 04.2 + TEDs, (3) corner crosses with capital letters + adjacent '↔' + TEDs, or (4) two boundary lines with capital letters + adjacent '↔' + TEDs. The leader line SHALL terminate directly on the restricted area. Multiple restricted areas are independent by default unless CZ is indicated.
rules.pass_condition: Restricted region uses ISO 128-24 type 04.2 (or lettered boundaries + ↔), exact TEDs locate/size the boundary, and the leader terminates squarely on the restricted area.
rules.fail_condition: Restricted portion is sketched with non-standard dashed lines, lacks TEDs locating the boundary, or the leader arrow points outside the demarcated zone.
rules.remediation: Demarcate the restricted area using ISO 128-24 type 04.2 wide chain lines (or lettered boundaries + ↔) with boxed TEDs and terminate the leader inside/on the restricted area.

rules.title: Continuous Non-Closed Compound Feature Indication ('Between' A↔B or Type 04.2)
rules.audit_check: A continuous non-closed compound toleranced feature SHALL have its start and end limits clearly identified either by an ISO 128-24 type 04.2 outline or by capital letters with arrowheads (and boxed TEDs if the limit does not fall on a natural integral feature boundary) paired with the adjacent 'between' indication (e.g., A↔B). The leader line SHALL terminate on the compound feature; constituent features are evaluated independently by default unless CZ or UF is indicated.
rules.pass_condition: Start and end points A and B are unambiguously indicated with arrows (and TEDs if mid-surface), 'A↔B' appears adjacent to the tolerance indicator, and CZ/UF/SZ clarifies combination intent.
rules.fail_condition: 'Between' uses retired '→' arrow (A.3.2), boundary letters are missing on the drawing view, or an intermediate stop point lacks a locating TED.
rules.remediation: Mark start/end limits with lettered arrows (plus TEDs if mid-feature), add 'A↔B' adjacent to the tolerance indicator, and specify CZ or UF if simultaneous evaluation is needed.

rules.title: Moveable Assembly Indications Governed by ISO/TS 17863
rules.audit_check: Geometrical tolerances on drawings of moveable assemblies SHOULD follow the specialized indication conventions of ISO/TS 17863.
rules.pass_condition: Moveable assembly drawings reference and follow ISO/TS 17863.
rules.fail_condition: Ad-hoc prose notes describe moveable-joint inspection configurations ambiguously.
rules.remediation: Standardize moveable assembly geometric indications in accordance with ISO/TS 17863.

rules.title: Collection Plane May Be Omitted for All-Around Line Profile Only When Identical to Intersection Plane
rules.audit_check: For a Line Profile (⌒) 'all around' specification, if the Collection Plane is IDENTICAL to the Intersection Plane, the Collection Plane indicator MAY be omitted (only the Intersection Plane indicator is required); if they differ, BOTH SHALL appear with Intersection Plane left of Collection Plane.
rules.pass_condition: All-around line profile either uses one Intersection Plane indicator (when planes coincide) or Intersection Plane followed immediately by Collection Plane.
rules.fail_condition: All-around line profile reverses Collection Plane and Intersection Plane order, or omits both planes.
rules.remediation: Include the Intersection Plane indicator (and add a separate Collection Plane to its right whenever the collection plane differs from the intersection plane).

rules.title: Explicit Limit Arrows & TEDs When A↔B Start/End Does Not Coincide With Integral Edge
rules.audit_check: When a start or end point (A or B) of a 'between' (A↔B) specification falls INSIDE a continuous surface rather than at a natural geometric boundary (corner/edge/tangent transition), its exact location SHALL be fixed by boxed TEDs and boundary indicators (per Fig. 62).
rules.pass_condition: Mid-surface start/end limits for A↔B are precisely located using boxed TEDs and crisp limit arrows/crosses.
rules.fail_condition: A boundary letter arrow (A or B) points vaguely into the middle of a surface with no TED fixing its position.
rules.remediation: Add boxed TEDs locating any mid-surface A↔B boundary points.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: TEDs Enclosed in Rectangular Frame and Never Directly Toleranced
rules.audit_check: Explicit Theoretically Exact Dimensions (TEDs) defining theoretical exact location, orientation, angle, or profile geometry SHALL be enclosed in a rectangular frame and SHALL NOT carry any direct ± tolerance (nor be subject to general tolerances).
rules.pass_condition: All explicit TEDs sit inside clean rectangular boxes with zero direct tolerance attached.
rules.fail_condition: A boxed TED includes a ± tolerance, or a dimension defining an angularity angle, position coordinate, or profile contour is left unboxed with a ± tolerance.
rules.remediation: Enclose exact nominal defining dimensions in rectangular TED frames and remove any direct ± tolerance from them.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Mandatory Title Block Note When TEDs Are Defined by a 3D CAD Model
rules.audit_check: When TEDs defining complex surfaces or features are NOT explicitly drawn as boxed dimensions on the 2D views and instead must be extracted from an associated 3D CAD model, an explicit indication SHALL appear near the title block (e.g., 'TEDs according to CAD model <filename/revision>').
rules.pass_condition: Drawings relying on CAD nominal data for profile/position tolerances include a clear title-block note citing the authoritative CAD model ID and revision.
rules.fail_condition: Profile or position tolerances appear on undimensioned contoured surfaces with no boxed TEDs AND no CAD-model TED declaration near the title block.
rules.remediation: Add explicit boxed TEDs to the drawing or place a clear 'TEDs according to CAD model <ID/Rev>' note near the title block.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Linear (/L) and Circular (/⌀d) Restrictive Specifications Evaluate Sliding Sub-Portions
rules.audit_check: In a restrictive specification ('t/L' for any linear length L, or 't/⌀d' for any circular area of diameter d), the tolerance applies over EVERY possible sub-portion of that extent anywhere on the feature, and per ISO 8015 ONLY the restricted portion is considered when associating the reference feature (usually paired with an overall full-feature tolerance above it).
rules.pass_condition: Restrictive specifications ('t/L' or 't/⌀d') are paired with an overall coarser full-feature tolerance when global bow/warp must also be limited.
rules.fail_condition: A restrictive tolerance ('0,05/100') is applied alone on a long rail or large mounting face without an overall full-length tolerance, unintentionally permitting unbounded cumulative bow across the full part.
rules.remediation: Stack an overall full-feature tolerance above the tighter restrictive local tolerance if global form/orientation must also be controlled.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Mandatory Orientation Plane Indicator for Rectangular Restrictive Specification (/L×H)
rules.audit_check: When a restrictive specification defines a rectangular area ('t/L×H', e.g., '0,05/50×100'), an Orientation Plane indicator (Clause 14) SHALL be added to define the direction of the FIRST dimension (L), unless L and H are equal and orientation is explicitly unconstrained (or specified).
rules.pass_condition: Every non-square rectangular restrictive specification ('/L×H') includes a valid Clause 14 orientation plane indicator establishing the direction of L.
rules.fail_condition: A rectangular restrictive area ('0,05/50×100') omits an orientation plane indicator, leaving the 50 vs 100 orientation undefined.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 14 orientation plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator to fix the direction of the first extent value (L).

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Cylindrical (/L×angle°) and Spherical (/angle1°×angle2°) Restrictive Area Rules
rules.audit_check: Cylindrical restricted portions SHALL be indicated as '/L×angle°' (axial length first, angular sector second). Spherical restricted portions SHALL be indicated as '/angle1°×angle2°' and SHALL include an orientation plane indicator defining the first angular direction. Restrictive extents are evaluated by orthogonal projection onto the nominal feature.
rules.pass_condition: Cylindrical extents put axial length before angle ('/50×30°'), and spherical extents ('/30°×45°') include an orientation plane indicator.
rules.fail_condition: Cylindrical extent reverses angle and length ('/30°×50'), omits degree symbols '°', or spherical extent omits the required orientation plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Format cylindrical restricted extents as '/L×angle°' and add an orientation plane indicator to spherical '/angle1°×angle2°' extents.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Direct Projected Tolerance (Ⓟ): ISO 128-24 Type 05.1 Line, Ⓟ Before TED, and Default Origin
rules.audit_check: For DIRECT indication of a projected toleranced feature (Table 7): (a) the projected extent SHALL be drawn using a long-dashed double-dotted narrow line (ISO 128-24 type 05.1) outside the workpiece, (b) the minimum projected length SHALL be a boxed TED immediately preceded by Ⓟ, (c) Ⓟ SHALL also appear in compartment 7 of the tolerance indicator, and (d) any offset from the reference plane SHALL be defined by a TED. By default, the projection starts at the reference plane (first intersecting plane) and extends OUT of material.
rules.pass_condition: Direct Ⓟ callout shows phantom line type 05.1, Ⓟ before the boxed projection TED, and Ⓟ inside compartment 7 of the tolerance indicator.
rules.fail_condition: Direct Ⓟ omits the phantom projection line (making direction ambiguous on a through-hole), uses a ± tolerance instead of a boxed TED for the projection length, or omits Ⓟ from compartment 7.
rules.remediation: Draw the projected axis/feature with ISO 128-24 type 05.1 line, prefix the boxed projection length TED with Ⓟ, and place Ⓟ in compartment 7 of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Indirect Projected Tolerance (Ⓟ25 / Ⓟ32-7) Restricted EXCLUSIVELY to Blind Holes
rules.audit_check: INDIRECT indication of a projected toleranced feature (placing the projection length directly in compartment 7, e.g., 'Ⓟ25' or 'Ⓟ32-7' with no phantom line) SHALL ONLY be used for BLIND HOLES (where projection direction out of the open mouth is unambiguous). In 'Ⓟa-b', 'a' is the farthest limit from the entry plane and 'b' is the nearest limit (offset; projected length = a − b). When the offset is zero, BOTH the zero AND the minus sign SHALL be omitted (e.g., 'Ⓟ25', NEVER 'Ⓟ25-0').
rules.pass_condition: Indirect 'Ⓟa' or 'Ⓟa-b' appears exclusively on blind holes (e.g., blind tapped/dowel holes), with zero offset written simply as 'Ⓟa'.
rules.fail_condition: Indirect 'Ⓟ25' is used on a THROUGH-HOLE (ambiguous which side the tolerance projects from!), or zero offset is written as 'Ⓟ25-0', or 'b' is larger than 'a'.
rules.remediation: Switch through-holes to DIRECT indication (type 05.1 phantom line + Ⓟ TED) so the projection side is unmistakable, and omit '-0' when offset is zero.

rules.section: Clauses 10, 11, and 12: TEDs, Restrictive Specifications, and Projected Features
rules.title: Orthogonal Projection of Restrictive Extents Yields Larger Curvilinear Length/Area on Curved Features
rules.audit_check: Because restrictive extents (/L, /L×H, /⌀d) are defined by ORTHOGONAL projection onto the nominal feature, the actual curvilinear arc length or surface area evaluated on a curved/sloped feature is LARGER than the indicated nominal extent (equal only when the feature is straight/flat).
rules.pass_condition: Restrictive extents on strongly curved surfaces account for orthogonal-projection enlargement (or use angular extents /L×θ° or /θ1°×θ2° on cylinders/spheres).
rules.fail_condition: A linear or rectangular restrictive extent (/L or /L×H) is applied across a steeply curved surface where orthogonal projection becomes undefined or severely distorted.
rules.remediation: Use cylindrical (/L×θ°) or spherical (/θ1°×θ2°) restrictive extents on cylinders/spheres, or verify orthogonal projection remains unambiguous on gently curved profiles.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Auxiliary Indicators Restricted to Revolute, Cylindrical, or Planar Datum Features Only
rules.audit_check: Per Clauses 13.2, 14.2, 15.2, and 16.2, ONLY revolute surfaces (cones, cylinders, tori with an axis), cylindrical surfaces, or planar surfaces (integral or median planes) SHALL be used as the datum feature inside an Intersection Plane, Orientation Plane, Direction Feature, or Collection Plane indicator. Points, spheres, or sculpted free-form surfaces SHALL NOT be referenced in auxiliary indicators.
rules.pass_condition: Every datum letter inside any auxiliary plane/feature indicator corresponds to a revolute, cylindrical, or planar datum feature.
rules.fail_condition: An auxiliary indicator references a spherical datum (point), a datum target point, or a free-form complex datum.
rules.remediation: Reference only a valid revolute, cylindrical, or planar datum inside intersection, orientation, direction, or collection plane indicators.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Mandatory Intersection Plane for Integral Lines (With Cylinder/Cone/Sphere Exceptions)
rules.audit_check: An Intersection Plane indicator SHALL be used whenever the toleranced feature is a set of integral lines on a surface — EXCEPT for straightness of generatrices of a cylinder/cone or roundness of a cylinder/cone/sphere (where the intersection plane family is inherently defined by the nominal revolute axis/center).
rules.pass_condition: All line-on-plane straightness/parallelism and line-profile callouts include an explicit Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A line profile or planar straightness tolerance omits the Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Attach a Clause 13 Intersection Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Table 8 Intersection Plane Validity Matrix (∥ to Revolute Axis & ⌯ to Plane Prohibited)
rules.audit_check: Per Clause 13.3–13.4 and Table 8, an Intersection Plane indicator uses ONLY symbols ∥ (parallel), ⊥ (perpendicular), ∠ (inclined + explicit TED angle), or ⌯ (symmetrical/containing the axis). Two combinations are STRICTLY PROHIBITED (Not Applicable): (1) ∥ (parallel to) an axis of a revolute surface (infinite plane orientations!), and (2) ⌯ (symmetrical/including) a plane.
rules.pass_condition: Intersection plane indicators use ⊥, ∠ (+ TED), or ⌯ with a revolute axis, OR ∥, ⊥, or ∠ (+ TED) with a datum plane.
rules.fail_condition: An intersection plane indicator specifies [∥|A] where A is a cylindrical/conical axis, [⌯|B] where B is a plane, or [∠|A] without an explicit boxed TED angle.
rules.remediation: Use [⌯|A] to define planes containing a revolute axis (instead of ∥), use [∥|B] for planes parallel to a datum plane (instead of ⌯), and add a boxed TED angle whenever ∠ is used.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Orientation Plane Datum Constrained Only by Preceding Datums in Tolerance Indicator
rules.audit_check: If the datum referenced inside an Orientation Plane indicator ALSO appears in the tolerance indicator's datum section, that datum is constrained ONLY by the datums preceding it in the tolerance indicator (Clause 14.4).
rules.pass_condition: Datum precedence in the tolerance indicator is consistent with the orientation plane's intended physical alignment.
rules.fail_condition: Orientation plane references a secondary or tertiary datum whose orientation conflicts with a primary datum constraining it.
rules.remediation: Verify that the datum hierarchy in the tolerance indicator matches the intended orientation plane alignment.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Table 9 Orientation Plane Validity Matrix (∥ to Revolute for Parallel Planes & ∥ to Plane for Cylinder Prohibited)
rules.audit_check: Per Clause 14.3–14.4 and Table 9, an Orientation Plane indicator uses ONLY ∥ (0°), ⊥ (90°), or ∠ (explicit TED angle ≠ 0°/90°). Two combinations are STRICTLY PROHIBITED (Not Applicable): (1) [∥|axis] for a two-parallel-planes tolerance zone (plane normal not fixed!), and (2) [∥|plane] for a cylindrical tolerance zone (cylinder axis not fixed!).
rules.pass_condition: Two-parallel-planes zones use ⊥/∠ with a revolute axis or ∥/⊥/∠ with a datum plane; cylindrical point zones use ∥/⊥/∠ with a revolute axis or ⊥/∠ with a datum plane; ∠ always has an explicit boxed TED angle.
rules.fail_condition: Orientation plane specifies [∥|axis] for a two-parallel-planes zone, [∥|plane] for a cylindrical zone, uses ⌯/↗, or uses ∠ without an explicit TED angle.
rules.remediation: Replace the invalid Table 9 combination with a geometrically constraining datum/symbol pair and ensure ∠ always has a boxed TED angle.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Mandatory Direction Feature Indicator for Non-Normal Integral Width or Conical Roundness
rules.audit_check: A Direction Feature indicator SHALL be used whenever: (a) the tolerance zone width for an integral feature is NOT normal to the specified nominal geometry, OR (b) a roundness specification is applied to a revolute surface that is neither cylindrical nor spherical (e.g., cone). In 2D, the leader arrow direction defines the zone width direction ONLY if explicitly constrained by a boxed TED angle (even if that angle is 90°!).
rules.pass_condition: Non-normal integral zone widths and non-cylindrical/non-spherical roundness callouts always carry a valid Clause 15 Direction Feature indicator (or in 2D, an explicit boxed TED angle on the leader line).
rules.fail_condition: A conical roundness callout omits a Direction Feature indicator, or a 2D non-normal measurement relies on an unboxed/unangled 90° leader arrow.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 15 Direction Feature indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator (or add an explicit boxed TED angle to the 2D leader line).

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Table 10 Direction Feature Matrix (Run-Out Symbol ↗ Prohibited on Planes & Restricted to Self-Datum)
rules.audit_check: Per Clause 15.3–15.4 and Table 10, a Direction Feature indicator uses ∥ (0°), ⊥ (90°), ∠ (explicit TED angle), or ↗ (perpendicular to surface of toleranced feature). Two strict prohibitions apply: (1) ↗ with a datum PLANE is NOT APPLICABLE, and (2) per Table 10 Footnote a, ↗ SHALL ONLY be used with the TOLERANCED FEATURE ITSELF indicated as the datum (and the direction is defined by the surface itself, NOT its derived axis).
rules.pass_condition: Direction feature indicators with ↗ reference exclusively a datum letter attached directly to the toleranced revolute surface itself; ∥/⊥/∠ follow Table 10 with explicit TED for ∠.
rules.fail_condition: Direction feature uses [↗|B] where B is a plane or a different feature than the toleranced feature, or uses ∠ without an explicit boxed TED angle.
rules.remediation: For normal-to-surface conical roundness, label the conical surface itself as a datum (e.g., A) and indicate [↗|A]; for axial/radial direction relative to another datum, use ∥, ⊥, or ∠ (+ TED).

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Collection Plane Syntax Follows Intersection Plane Rules (Table 8)
rules.audit_check: A Collection Plane indicator SHALL be placed as the rightmost auxiliary indicator (after any Intersection Plane or Orientation/Direction indicator) whenever 'all around' is used in 3D (and preferred in 2D), using the same graphical symbols (∥, ⊥, ∠ + TED, ⌯) and invariance prohibitions as Table 8.
rules.pass_condition: Collection plane sits rightmost with zero gap, references a valid revolute/cylindrical/planar datum, and obeys Table 8 symbol validity.
rules.fail_condition: Collection plane uses [∥|axis], [⌯|plane], omits a TED with ∠, or is placed to the left of an Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Position the Collection Plane indicator rightmost with zero gap and use a valid Table 8 symbol + datum combination.

rules.section: Clauses 13, 14, 15, and 16: Auxiliary Plane and Feature Indicators (Tables 8–10)
rules.title: Symmetry Symbol (⌯) Inside Intersection/Collection Plane Means Plane Contains Datum Axis
rules.audit_check: Inside an Intersection Plane or Collection Plane indicator, the symmetry symbol ⌯ specifically designates planes that INCLUDE (contain / are symmetrical around) the referenced datum axis (e.g., axial longitudinal sections of a cone or cylinder) — never use ∥ for this purpose.
rules.pass_condition: [⌯|A] is used cleanly whenever radial/longitudinal planes containing datum axis A are required.
rules.fail_condition: [∥|A] is mistakenly written to specify longitudinal planes containing cylinder/cone axis A.
rules.remediation: Replace [∥|A] with [⌯|A] whenever intersection or collection planes must contain datum axis A.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Straightness: Integral Line vs Derived Median Line Zone Shapes & Indicators
rules.audit_check: Straightness (⏤) SHALL reference NO datum. On an integral planar surface, straightness SHALL include an Intersection Plane indicator (13.4). On a derived median line, straightness uses EITHER a cylindrical zone (⌀ prefix) OR two parallel planes requiring an Orientation Plane indicator (7.3) — or two perpendicular parallel-planes zones each with an Orientation Plane.
rules.pass_condition: Integral cylinder/cone generatrix straightness attaches to outline; planar-line straightness includes an intersection plane; median-line straightness uses ⌀ or an orientation plane.
rules.fail_condition: Straightness includes a datum, applies to a flat surface without an intersection plane, or applies to a median line without ⌀ and without an orientation plane.
rules.remediation: Remove any datum, add an intersection plane for planar lines, and add ⌀ or an orientation plane indicator for derived median lines.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Flatness Restricted to Integral Planar Surfaces Only (No Datum, No ⌀, No Ⓜ)
rules.audit_check: Flatness (⏥) defines a zone limited by two parallel planes distance t apart and SHALL ONLY be applied to an integral nominally planar surface (or united/combined planar surfaces with UF/CZ), with NO datum, NO ⌀/S⌀ prefix, NO Ⓐ, and NO Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.pass_condition: Flatness leader terminates cleanly on a planar surface outline/extension/dot (separated from any dimension line) with no datum or FOS modifiers.
rules.fail_condition: Flatness is applied to a derived median plane (aligned with thickness dimension line), a curved surface, includes ⌀ or Ⓜ, or references a datum.
rules.remediation: Attach flatness strictly to the integral planar surface (offset from dimension lines) and remove invalid datums or FOS modifiers (use Straightness/Position for median planes).

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Roundness on Cylinders, Spheres, and Non-Cylindrical Revolutes
rules.audit_check: Roundness (○) controls each cross-sectional integral circle of a revolute surface (two concentric circles radial width t, NO datum, NO ⌀ prefix). For cylinders and spheres, the zone width defaults perpendicular to the axis/center. For ALL other revolutes (cones, tapers, tori), a Direction Feature indicator SHALL ALWAYS be specified (7.1, 15.1).
rules.pass_condition: Roundness attaches to the integral revolute surface without datum or ⌀, and every conical/non-cylindrical/non-spherical roundness includes a Direction Feature indicator.
rules.fail_condition: Roundness includes a ⌀ prefix or datum, attaches to a dimension line extension, or applies to a cone without a Direction Feature indicator.
rules.remediation: Remove ⌀ and any datum, offset leader from dimension line, and attach a Direction Feature indicator for conical/tapered roundness.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Cylindricity Restricted Exclusively to Integral Cylindrical Surfaces
rules.audit_check: Cylindricity (⌭) defines two coaxial cylinders radial distance t apart and SHALL ONLY be applied to an integral nominally cylindrical surface, with NO datum, NO ⌀ prefix, NO Ⓐ, and NO Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.pass_condition: Cylindricity targets an integral cylindrical surface cleanly offset from diameter dimension lines, with no datum or ⌀/Ⓜ modifiers.
rules.fail_condition: Cylindricity is applied to a cone, sphere, or derived axis, includes ⌀ or Ⓜ, or references a datum.
rules.remediation: Apply cylindricity solely to integral cylinders (use Surface Profile without datum for conical form) and remove any datum, ⌀, or Ⓜ.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Line Profile Without Datum Controls Form Only and Requires TEDs + Intersection Plane
rules.audit_check: Line profile (⌒) without a datum controls pure form of each integral line profile (enveloped by circles of diameter t centered on the TEF). The nominal profile shape SHALL be defined by boxed TEDs (or CAD reference; unless OZ/VA frees linear/angular offset), and an Intersection Plane indicator SHALL define the cutting plane family.
rules.pass_condition: Datumless line profile includes an Intersection Plane indicator and complete nominal profile TEDs (or OZ/VA where size/angle varies).
rules.fail_condition: Line profile omits an Intersection Plane indicator or uses ± toleranced profile dimensions without OZ/VA.
rules.remediation: Add an Intersection Plane indicator and enclose all defining nominal profile dimensions in TED boxes (or add OZ/VA).

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Datum-Referenced Line Profile Controls Location, Orientation, and Form (Unless >< Specified)
rules.audit_check: Line profile (⌒) referencing a datum system controls location, orientation, and form simultaneously relative to those datums (unless >< in compartment 4 frees translation for orientation-only control), and SHALL have boxed TEDs relating the nominal profile to the referenced datums plus an Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.pass_condition: Boxed TEDs link the nominal profile to all referenced datums (except unconstrained DOFs or ><), and an Intersection Plane indicator is present.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions locating the profiled line from the referenced datums carry ± tolerances instead of TED boxes.
rules.remediation: Convert locating/orienting dimensions between datums and the profiled line into boxed TEDs and include an Intersection Plane indicator.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Surface Profile Without Datum Controls Form of Nominal Surface (TEDs or CAD Reference)
rules.audit_check: Surface profile (⌓) without a datum defines a tolerance zone enveloped by spheres of diameter t centered on the nominal TEF surface (pure form). The nominal surface geometry SHALL be unambiguously defined by boxed TEDs or an explicit CAD model TED reference note (unless OZ/VA frees linear/angular offset).
rules.pass_condition: Datumless surface profile has fully defined nominal surface TEDs (or CAD note) and uses CZ/UF if spanning multiple surfaces.
rules.fail_condition: Datumless surface profile applies to an undimensioned curve without a CAD TED note, or has conflicting ± form dimensions without OZ/VA.
rules.remediation: Box nominal defining dimensions as TEDs (or cite the 3D CAD model for TEDs near the title block) and add OZ/VA if size/angle is separately controlled.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Datum-Referenced Surface Profile and Orientation-Only Refinement (><)
rules.audit_check: Surface profile (⌓) related to a datum system constrains location, orientation, and form relative to all DOFs locked by those datums (requiring boxed TEDs from the datums). When orientation-only profile refinement is desired relative to datums (freeing translation), >< SHALL be placed in compartment 4 (or stacked below a wider location surface profile).
rules.pass_condition: All dimensions relating the profiled surface to the datum system are boxed TEDs (or CAD-defined), and orientation-only refinements explicitly use >< in compartment 4.
rules.fail_condition: Locating dimensions between datums and a datum-referenced surface profile carry ± tolerances, or a stacked tighter profile omits >< when translation freedom was intended.
rules.remediation: Box all locating/orienting dimensions from the datum system as TEDs, and add >< in compartment 4 for orientation-only profile refinements.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Parallelism Rules Across Median Lines, Integral Lines, and Planar Surfaces (17.10.1–17.10.7)
rules.audit_check: Parallelism (∥) SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum (line, plane, or datum system) with implicit 0° TED. For a median line related to a datum line/system without ⌀ (two parallel planes), an Orientation Plane indicator SHALL be specified (17.10.2–17.10.3). For a set of integral lines on a surface parallel to a datum plane (17.10.5), an Intersection Plane indicator SHALL be specified. For a planar surface (17.10.6–17.10.7), NO ⌀ prefix is permitted.
rules.pass_condition: Parallelism references a valid datum, uses ⌀ only on derived median lines, includes an orientation plane for parallel-planes median-line zones, and includes an intersection plane for integral lines on a surface.
rules.fail_condition: Parallelism omits a datum, applies ⌀ to a planar surface, or omits an orientation/intersection plane where required by 17.10.2–17.10.5.
rules.remediation: Add the required datum and auxiliary plane indicator (orientation plane for parallel-planes median line; intersection plane for integral surface lines), and remove ⌀ from planes.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Perpendicularity Rules (Implicit 90° TED, Median Line vs Planar Surface, 17.11.1–17.11.6)
rules.audit_check: Perpendicularity (⊥) enforces an implicit 90° TED and SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum (line, plane, or datum system). A median line perpendicular to a datum plane typically uses a cylindrical zone (⌀) — if ⌀ is omitted (two parallel planes), an Orientation Plane indicator SHALL be specified (17.11.2–17.11.4). Planar surface perpendicularity (17.11.5–17.11.6) SHALL NOT use ⌀.
rules.pass_condition: Perpendicularity targets a valid 90° nominal relationship with a datum, uses ⌀ for omnidirectional hole/pin squareness (or includes an orientation plane for single-direction control), and never applies ⌀ to a plane.
rules.fail_condition: Hole/shaft perpendicularity to a datum plane omits BOTH ⌀ AND an orientation plane indicator, or planar perpendicularity carries ⌀.
rules.remediation: Add ⌀ for omnidirectional cylindrical squareness (or add an orientation plane indicator for planar-zone control) and ensure nominal geometry is 90°.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Angularity Mandatory Explicit Boxed TED Angle (≠ 0°/90°) and Datum (17.12.1–17.12.5)
rules.audit_check: Angularity (∠) SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum/datum system AND SHALL ALWAYS be accompanied by an EXPLICIT boxed TED angle between the toleranced feature and the datum (never a ± toleranced angle). For a median line with a two-parallel-planes zone, an Orientation Plane indicator SHALL be specified (17.12.2–17.12.3).
rules.pass_condition: Angularity references a valid datum, the nominal angle is enclosed in a rectangular TED frame, and any non-cylindrical median-line zone includes an orientation plane.
rules.fail_condition: The angle for an angularity tolerance has a ± tolerance instead of a TED box, or the datum is omitted.
rules.remediation: Enclose the nominal angle in a rectangular TED box (removing any ± tolerance) and verify the required datum and orientation plane indicator.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Position Rules for Derived Points, Median Lines, Median Planes, and Planar Surfaces (17.13.1–17.13.5)
rules.audit_check: Position (⌖) requires explicit or implicit TEDs locating the toleranced feature (derived point, median line, median plane, or integral planar surface) relative to its datum system (or within a pattern per ISO 5458). Specifically: (a) spherical point zones require S⌀, cylindrical axis/point zones require ⌀ (cylindrical point zone ALSO requires an Orientation Plane); (b) median-line two-parallel-planes zones require an Orientation Plane; (c) planar surface position (17.13.5) applies to an integral plane (NO ⌀, NO Ⓜ) and is the ONLY position case allowing UZ.
rules.pass_condition: All locating dimensions are boxed TEDs, ⌀/S⌀ prefixes and orientation planes match feature type, and UZ/Ⓜ rules are strictly respected.
rules.fail_condition: Position locating dimensions carry ± tolerances instead of TED boxes, hole position omits ⌀ without an orientation plane, or Ⓜ/UZ is misused.
rules.remediation: Box all locating dimensions as TEDs, add ⌀ (or S⌀ / orientation plane as applicable), and restrict UZ to integral planar surfaces and Ⓜ to features of size.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Concentricity (Derived Point + ACS) and Coaxiality (Derived Median Line + ⌀) Rules
rules.audit_check: Concentricity and Coaxiality (◎) SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum point or axis (implicit 0 mm TED) and apply ONLY to derived features (centre point or median line — aligned with dimension line or modified by Ⓐ). For concentricity of derived centre points of cross-sections of a revolute/cylindrical surface (17.14.1–17.14.2), the adjacent ACS identifier SHALL be indicated (and ⌀ precedes the circular zone value). Coaxiality of an axis (17.14.3) uses ⌀ for a cylindrical zone.
rules.pass_condition: ◎ references a coaxial/concentric datum, targets a derived feature (dimension line or Ⓐ), includes ⌀/S⌀, and includes ACS when specifying cross-sectional point concentricity.
rules.fail_condition: ◎ is attached to an integral outline without Ⓐ, omits ⌀/S⌀, omits a datum, or omits ACS when intending 2D cross-section concentricity on a cylinder/cone.
rules.remediation: Attach ◎ to the derived feature (dimension line or Ⓐ), prepend ⌀ (or S⌀ for sphere), add the datum, and add ACS for cross-sectional concentricity.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Symmetry Requires Derived Feature, Zero Linear TEDs, Translation-Locking Datum, and ACS for Points
rules.audit_check: Symmetry (⌯) applies ONLY to derived features (median plane, median line, or centre point — aligned with FOS dimension line or Ⓐ for revolutes), SHALL use ZERO linear offset TEDs (implicit 0 mm symmetry), SHALL reference a datum/datum system locking at least one translation degree of freedom, and SHALL include ACS when controlling cross-sectional centre points on a line (17.15.1). Symmetry SHALL NOT use ⌀ for a median plane.
rules.pass_condition: Symmetry targets a derived FOS median element centered nominally at 0 mm on a valid translation-locking datum plane/axis.
rules.fail_condition: Symmetry is applied to a non-FOS single plane, includes a non-zero offset TED, references a datum that locks no relevant translation, or attaches to an outline instead of the width dimension line.
rules.remediation: Align symmetry with the FOS width dimension line (or use Position if offset by a non-zero TED) and reference a datum plane/axis locking the symmetry translation.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Circular Run-Out Restricted to Integral Features With Datum Axis (Radial, Axial, Any, Specified Direction)
rules.audit_check: Circular run-out (↗) SHALL ONLY apply to INTEGRAL features (cylinders, planar faces, cones, curved revolutes — NEVER derived axes, NO ⌀, NO Ⓜ/Ⓛ) and SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum axis. Radial (17.16.2) applies perpendicular to datum axis on a cylinder; Axial (17.16.3) applies parallel to datum axis on a planar end face; Any direction (17.16.4) applies perpendicular to a conical/curved revolute surface by default; Specified direction (17.16.5) SHALL define the angled direction via a boxed TED angle or Direction Feature indicator.
rules.pass_condition: Circular run-out targets an integral surface of revolution/end face (leader offset from dimension lines), references a valid datum axis, omits ⌀ and Ⓜ/Ⓛ, and defines any non-default angle with a TED or Direction Feature.
rules.fail_condition: Circular run-out includes ⌀ or Ⓜ/Ⓛ, attaches to a diameter dimension line, references a datum plane alone (no axis), or implies an oblique direction without a TED/Direction Feature.
rules.remediation: Attach circular run-out cleanly to the integral surface, reference a datum axis (or common axis A-B), remove ⌀/Ⓜ/Ⓛ, and box any oblique measurement angle as a TED.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Total Run-Out Restricted to Integral Cylindrical (Radial) or Planar (Axial) Surfaces With Datum Axis
rules.audit_check: Total run-out (⌰) SHALL ONLY apply to INTEGRAL nominally cylindrical surfaces coaxial with the datum axis (radial, 17.17.2) OR nominally planar surfaces perpendicular to the datum axis (axial, 17.17.3), with NO ⌀ prefix and NO Ⓜ/Ⓛ modifiers, and SHALL ALWAYS reference a datum axis. (Cones/curved revolutes cannot use Total Run-out — use Surface Profile or Circular Run-out instead.)
rules.pass_condition: Total run-out targets an integral coaxial cylinder or perpendicular end face, references a valid datum axis, and omits ⌀ and Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.fail_condition: Total run-out is applied to a conical/curved surface, includes ⌀ or Ⓜ/Ⓛ, attaches to a dimension line, or lacks a datum axis.
rules.remediation: Restrict total run-out to integral coaxial cylinders or perpendicular planar faces (use Surface Profile or Circular Run-out for cones/curved revolutes) and remove any ⌀ or Ⓜ/Ⓛ.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Derived Centre Point of a Torus Cannot Be Specified Directly
rules.audit_check: Per Annex B.8, the derived centre point of a torus CANNOT be specified directly in ISO 1101:2017 (whereas its derived axis/median circle or integral surface profile can be controlled).
rules.pass_condition: Toroidal features are controlled via integral surface profile or valid derived-axis specifications rather than a direct torus centre-point callout.
rules.fail_condition: A tolerance indicator attempts to tolerance the single derived centre point of a toroidal surface.
rules.remediation: Control toroidal geometry using Surface Profile (⌓) or valid revolute-axis specifications.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Discontinuity Sphere/Circle (Radius 0.5×t) at Non-Smooth Profile Corners
rules.audit_check: Per Annex B.9, where a continuous toleranced profile has a sharp corner (tangent discontinuity), the tolerance zone automatically wraps around the exterior vertex with a circular/spherical arc of radius 0.5×t (permitting corner rounding up to 0.5×t unless a sharper edge/corner specification is explicitly added).
rules.pass_condition: Sharp-edge functional requirements (e.g., sealing edges or knife edges) carry an explicit edge-break/ISO 13715 callout in addition to profile, or rounding up to 0.5×t is acceptable.
rules.fail_condition: A mating sharp corner controlled solely by a wide UF/all-around profile tolerance relies on crisp corner geometry without an edge-condition tolerance.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit edge specification (ISO 13715) or split the profile tolerance at the sharp corner if 0.5×t corner rounding is functionally unacceptable.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Oblique Circular Run-Out Requires Explicit TED Angle or Direction Feature Indicator
rules.audit_check: Per Clause 17.16.4–17.16.5, circular run-out on a conical or curved revolute surface applies PERPENDICULAR to the surface by default ('any direction'). If measurement in a SPECIFIC non-normal direction (e.g., radial or axial on a cone, or an explicit angle α) is required, a Clause 15 Direction Feature indicator OR an explicit boxed TED angle on the 2D leader line SHALL be specified.
rules.pass_condition: Normal-to-surface conical circular run-out omits extra direction modifiers (default 17.16.4), while radial/axial/oblique conical circular run-out explicitly adds a Direction Feature indicator or boxed TED angle.
rules.fail_condition: Conical circular run-out draws a horizontal or vertical leader arrow expecting radial/axial measurement without a Direction Feature indicator or boxed TED angle.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 15 Direction Feature indicator (e.g., [⊥|A] for radial or [∥|A] for axial) or a boxed TED angle on the 2D leader line.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Pattern Features Require Complete Explicit/Implicit TED Network (No Toleranced Pitch Dimensions)
rules.audit_check: Per Annex B.3–B.6 and ISO 5458, all nominal distances, bolt-circle diameters, and angles defining the relative geometry of a pattern of toleranced features SHALL be explicit boxed TEDs (or implicit 0°/90°/180°/270°/360°÷n equal spacing), never ± toleranced pitch dimensions.
rules.pass_condition: Bolt-circle diameters, hole-to-hole linear pitches, and non-uniform angular pitches in a positioned pattern are all boxed TEDs.
rules.fail_condition: A bolt-circle diameter or hole-to-hole spacing carries a ± tolerance alongside a Position tolerance on the same pattern.
rules.remediation: Enclose all pattern pitch and bolt-circle dimensions in rectangular TED frames and remove conflicting ± tolerances.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: Datum System Must Lock Intended Non-Redundant Degrees of Freedom (No Redundant or Missing Datums)
rules.audit_check: Per Annex B.7 and B.10.3–B.10.4, every datum listed in a tolerance indicator's datum section SHOULD constrain at least one non-redundant degree of freedom of the tolerance zone, and all functionally required translations/rotations of the zone SHOULD be constrained by the datum system.
rules.pass_condition: Every primary/secondary/tertiary datum contributes meaningful non-redundant DOF constraint matching the part's functional assembly alignment.
rules.fail_condition: A datum compartment lists a redundant datum (e.g., parallelism of a plane to [A|B] where primary plane A already locks all rotational DOFs of the zone!) or omits a tertiary clocking datum needed for an asymmetric hole pattern.
rules.remediation: Remove redundant datums that lock zero additional DOFs of the tolerance zone, and add missing secondary/tertiary datums where clocking or translation must be constrained.

rules.section: Clause 17 & Annex B: Characteristic-Specific Rules and Zone Definitions
rules.title: ACS Applies Exclusively to Surfaces Whose Derived Feature Is a Straight Line (Revolute, Cylindrical, Prismatic)
rules.audit_check: Per Annex B.10.6, the Any Cross-Section (ACS) modifier defines cross-sections perpendicular to a straight derived line and SHALL ONLY be applied to revolute, cylindrical, or prismatic surfaces (never to spheres, tori without linear spine, or doubly curved free-form surfaces).
rules.pass_condition: Every ACS modifier appears strictly on a revolute, cylindrical, or prismatic feature.
rules.fail_condition: ACS is applied to a spherical, single-plane, or doubly curved sculpted feature.
rules.remediation: Remove ACS from invalid feature geometries and use an explicit Clause 13 Intersection Plane indicator instead.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Deprecated: Relying on Drawing Plane Instead of Explicit Intersection Plane Indicator
rules.audit_check: Relying implicitly on the 2D drawing projection plane to define the intersection plane for straightness, line profile, or line parallelism on a planar/sculpted surface is DEPRECATED (ISO 1101:2012 practice) and SHOULD be replaced with an explicit Clause 13 Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.pass_condition: All integral-line tolerances include an explicit Intersection Plane indicator rather than relying on the 2D view plane.
rules.fail_condition: A 2D line-profile, planar-straightness, or line-parallelism tolerance omits an Intersection Plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Attach a Clause 13 Intersection Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Deprecated: Obsolete 'LE' (Line Element) Modifier
rules.audit_check: The 'LE' (line element) modifier from ISO 1101:2012 is DEPRECATED and SHALL NOT be used on ISO 1101:2017 drawings; use an explicit Intersection Plane indicator (Clause 13) instead.
rules.pass_condition: No 'LE' modifier appears anywhere on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: The obsolete 'LE' modifier appears in or adjacent to any tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Remove 'LE' and add a Clause 13 Intersection Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Deprecated: Omitting Collection Plane Indicator in 2D 'All Around' Specifications
rules.audit_check: Omitting the Collection Plane indicator in a 2D 'all around' specification is DEPRECATED (A.2.3); drawings SHOULD include an explicit Clause 16 Collection Plane indicator (which is mandatory in 3D per 9.1.2).
rules.pass_condition: 2D 'all around' specifications include an explicit Clause 16 Collection Plane indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A 2D 'all around' (○) specification omits the Collection Plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 16 Collection Plane indicator to the right end of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Deprecated: Omitting Orientation Plane Indicator in 2D by Relying on Dimension Line Direction
rules.audit_check: Omitting the Orientation Plane indicator in 2D and relying on the graphical direction of the dimension line to orient a two-parallel-planes or cylindrical point tolerance zone is DEPRECATED (A.2.4) and SHOULD be replaced with an explicit Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator.
rules.pass_condition: All non-cylindrical derived median-line zones and cylindrical centre-point zones include an explicit Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A 2D median-line tolerance without ⌀ relies solely on dimension line direction without an Orientation Plane indicator.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator immediately to the right of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Obsolete 'NC' (Not Convex) Modifier
rules.audit_check: The 'NC' (not convex) modifier is an ambiguous FORMER practice from ISO 1101:2012 and SHALL NO LONGER be used on ISO 1101:2017 drawings.
rules.pass_condition: No 'NC' modifier appears anywhere on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: The obsolete 'NC' modifier appears in or near any tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Remove 'NC' and express functional concavity/form requirements using standardized profile, UZ, or reference-association/parameter modifiers.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Retired 'From...To' (→) Symbol Replaced by 'Between' (↔)
rules.audit_check: The single-headed 'from...to' symbol (→, e.g., 'A→B') is RETIRED (Foreword & A.3.2) and SHALL NO LONGER be used; the double-headed 'between' symbol (↔, e.g., 'A↔B') SHALL be used instead for both compound non-closed features and linearly variable tolerance zones.
rules.pass_condition: All start-to-end feature and variable-width callouts use the double-headed '↔' symbol.
rules.fail_condition: A single-headed arrow 'A→B' or text 'FROM A TO B' appears adjacent to a tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Replace 'A→B' (or 'FROM A TO B') with the standardized 'A↔B' between symbol (Fig. F.5).

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Omitting Direction Feature on Conical/Non-Cylindrical Roundness
rules.audit_check: Assuming by default that roundness on a cone or non-cylindrical/non-spherical revolute applies perpendicular to the axis without a Direction Feature indicator is a FORMER practice (A.3.3) and SHALL NOT be used under ISO 1101:2017 (7.1, 15.1).
rules.pass_condition: Every roundness callout on a cone or non-cylindrical/non-spherical revolute carries an explicit Direction Feature indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A conical roundness indicator lacks a Direction Feature indicator.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 15 Direction Feature indicator specifying perpendicular-to-axis ([⊥|A]) or perpendicular-to-surface ([↗|A]).

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Bare 'All Around' Without SZ, CZ, or UF
rules.audit_check: Indicating 'all around' (or 'all over') WITHOUT SZ, CZ, or UF (when datums do not lock all non-redundant DOFs) is an ambiguous FORMER practice (A.3.4) and SHALL NOT be used on ISO 1101:2017 drawings (9.1.2).
rules.pass_condition: All non-fully-constrained 'all around'/'all over' callouts explicitly include SZ, CZ, or UF.
rules.fail_condition: A datumless or partially constrained 'all around'/'all over' callout omits SZ, CZ, and UF.
rules.remediation: Explicitly add CZ, UF, or SZ to clarify whether the closed chain is evaluated simultaneously, as a united feature, or independently.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: 'Edge-to-Edge' Profile Interpretation Without UF
rules.audit_check: Interpreting a single-leader profile tolerance as automatically spanning 'from edge to edge' across multiple tangent surfaces (e.g., plane + fillet + cylinder) without UF or 'between' (A↔B) is a FORMER practice (A.3.5) and SHALL NOT be relied upon.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-segment tangent contours intended as a single profiled surface explicitly specify UF (with A↔B or all-around).
rules.fail_condition: A single leader line points to one segment of a blended contour expecting the profile to carry across tangent radii/planes without UF or A↔B.
rules.remediation: Add UF and 'A↔B' (or 'all around' + UF) to explicitly unite all intended tangent segments.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Leader Arrow Direction Defining Orientation of Median-Line/Centre-Point Zone
rules.audit_check: Using the graphical direction of the leader arrow alone to orient a tolerance zone for a centre point or median line in one direction is a FORMER practice (A.3.6) and SHALL NOT be used; use an explicit Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator instead.
rules.pass_condition: Single-direction median-line and centre-point tolerance zones explicitly specify a Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator.
rules.fail_condition: A leader arrow orientation is relied upon to define the direction of a non-⌀ median-line or centre-point tolerance zone.
rules.remediation: Add a Clause 14 Orientation Plane indicator to explicitly define the zone orientation.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Relying on Unstated Metrologist 'Common Practice' for Filtering
rules.audit_check: Relying on unstated metrologist 'common practice' for filtration (cutoff lengths/UPR) on functional precision form tolerances is a FORMER practice (A.3.7) that introduces inspection ambiguity; drawings SHOULD specify explicit filter elements (8.2.2.2.1) or drawing defaults (Table 6).
rules.pass_condition: Critical form specifications (e.g., bearing seats, sealing faces, precision shafts) explicitly declare filter type and cutoff or reference a Table 6 drawing default.
rules.fail_condition: Tight form tolerances (e.g., 0,005 roundness or 0,01 flatness) provide zero local or drawing-default filter guidance.
rules.remediation: Add explicit filter modifiers (e.g., G50- or G0,8-) or a drawing-wide 'ISO 1101 TFF:' default near the title block.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Ambiguous Datum Triangle on Cylinder Outline Instead of Dimension Line / Target
rules.audit_check: Placing a datum feature indicator directly on a cylindrical surface outline in a 2D view where it is ambiguous whether the cylinder axis or a single generatrix/surface is intended (instead of placing it on the extension of the diameter dimension line or using datum targets per ISO 5459) is a FORMER practice (A.3.8) and SHALL be avoided.
rules.pass_condition: Cylindrical datum triangles sit cleanly on the extension of the diameter dimension line (or on the integral cylinder per unambiguous ISO 5459 3D/2D rules without outline ambiguity).
rules.fail_condition: A datum triangle rests ambiguously on the side outline of a cylinder in a 2D orthographic view.
rules.remediation: Move the cylindrical datum feature triangle to align with the diameter dimension line (or specify explicit datum targets per ISO 5459).

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Square Brackets Around UZ Offset Value (e.g., UZ[+0,2])
rules.audit_check: Enclosing the offset value after UZ in square brackets (e.g., 'UZ[+0,2]' or 'UZ[-0,1]') is a FORMER practice from ISO 1101:2012 (A.3.9) and SHALL NO LONGER be used; write the signed value directly after UZ with no brackets (e.g., 'UZ+0,2').
rules.pass_condition: All UZ offsets appear cleanly without square brackets (e.g., '0,4 UZ+0,2').
rules.fail_condition: Square brackets appear around any UZ offset value (e.g., 'UZ[+0,2]').
rules.remediation: Remove the square brackets so the specification reads 'UZ+val' or 'UZ-val'.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Legacy Terminology 'Profile Any Line' / 'Profile Any Surface'
rules.audit_check: Using the legacy terms 'profile any line' or 'profile any surface' in drawing notes or inspection schedules is a FORMER practice (A.3.10); drawings SHOULD use 'line profile' and 'surface profile' per Table 2.
rules.pass_condition: Notes and tables use 'line profile' and 'surface profile'.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing text contains 'profile any line' or 'profile any surface'.
rules.remediation: Update legacy terminology to 'line profile' and 'surface profile'.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Tolerance Leader Arrow Connected Directly to Axis/Centerline or Median Plane
rules.audit_check: Connecting a tolerance indicator leader arrow directly to a centerline, axis, or median plane is an obsolete FORMER practice from ISO 1101:1983 (A.4.1) and SHALL NOT be used — because centerlines can belong to multiple coaxial/symmetrical features ambiguously.
rules.pass_condition: Zero tolerance indicator leaders terminate on centerlines or axes; all derived-feature tolerances attach to the FOS dimension line extension or use Ⓐ (revolutes only).
rules.fail_condition: Any tolerance indicator leader arrowhead touches a centerline/axis.
rules.remediation: Re-attach the leader arrowhead to the extension of the specific feature's size dimension line, or add Ⓐ (revolutes only) and point to the specific surface/outline.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Datum Triangle Connected Directly to Axis/Centerline or Median Plane
rules.audit_check: Attaching a datum feature triangle and letter directly to a centerline, axis, or median plane is an obsolete FORMER practice from ISO 1101:1983 (A.4.2) and SHALL NOT be used.
rules.pass_condition: All datum feature triangles attach strictly to feature outlines/surfaces (integral datums) or extensions of size dimension lines (derived FOS datums) per ISO 5459.
rules.fail_condition: Any datum feature triangle touches a centerline or axis.
rules.remediation: Move the datum triangle to align with the specific Feature of Size dimension line (or to the specific integral datum surface).

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Unordered Datum Letters Without Precedence or Hyphen ('AB')
rules.audit_check: Placing multiple datum letters inside a single datum compartment without an order of precedence or hyphen (e.g., '[AB]') is an obsolete FORMER practice from ISO 1101:1983 (A.4.3) and SHALL NOT be used.
rules.pass_condition: Sequential datums occupy separate compartments ('[A|B]'), and simultaneous common datums use a hyphen ('[A-B]').
rules.fail_condition: Two or more datum letters appear unhyphenated inside the same compartment (e.g., '[AB]' or '[A B]').
rules.remediation: Split into separate compartments '[A|B]' with defined precedence, or join with a hyphen '[A-B]' if a simultaneous common datum is intended.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Tolerance Indicator Connected Directly to Datum Feature Without Datum Letter
rules.audit_check: Connecting a tolerance indicator directly to a datum feature via a leader line terminating in a datum triangle (omitting the datum letter compartment) is an obsolete FORMER practice from ISO 1101:1983 (A.4.4) and SHALL NOT be used.
rules.pass_condition: Every datum is explicitly named with a capital letter inside a datum feature indicator and referenced by letter in the tolerance indicator's datum section.
rules.fail_condition: A datum triangle leader connects directly from a feature to a tolerance indicator frame without a datum letter.
rules.remediation: Assign an explicit datum letter (e.g., A) to the datum feature indicator and reference that letter in the tolerance indicator's datum compartment.

rules.section: Annex A: Deprecated and Former Practices (ISO 1101:2012 & ISO 1101:1983)
rules.title: Former Practice: Text Label 'Common Zone' Instead of Standardized 'CZ' Modifier
rules.audit_check: Writing the text label 'common zone' (or 'COMMON ZONE') adjacent to a tolerance indicator instead of placing the standardized 'CZ' modifier inside compartment 2 is an obsolete FORMER practice from ISO 1101:1983 (A.4.5) and SHALL NOT be used.
rules.pass_condition: Combined tolerance zones are specified exclusively using the 'CZ' modifier inside compartment 2 of the tolerance indicator.
rules.fail_condition: Text 'common zone' appears above, below, or beside a tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Delete the 'common zone' text and insert 'CZ' in compartment 2 of the tolerance indicator.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Exclusive Use of Valid Table C.1 Filter Symbols
visual_syntax_triggers: Table C.1 (G, S, SW, CW, RG, RS, OB, OH, OD, CB, CH, CD, AB, AH, AD, F, H)
rules.audit_check: Any filter modifier in compartment 5a (or Table 6 drawing defaults) SHALL use one of the 17 standardized Table C.1 symbols: linear/robust (G, S, SW, CW, RG, RS), morphological (OB, OH, OD, CB, CH, CD, AB, AH, AD), Fourier (F), or Hull (H).
rules.pass_condition: Every filter symbol matches an exact Table C.1 code.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard filter abbreviations (e.g., 'GAUSS', '2RC', 'LPF', 'MORPH') appear in tolerance indicators.
rules.remediation: Replace non-standard filter text with the corresponding Table C.1 filter symbol.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Table C.2 Nesting Index Semantics (Cutoff mm/UPR, Radius, Segment Length, H0 Convex Hull)
rules.audit_check: Filter nesting indices SHALL match Table C.2 definitions: cutoff length (mm) for open profiles or cutoff UPR for closed profiles (G, S, SW, CW, RG, RS); ball/disc radius (mm) for OB/CB/AB/OD/CD/AD; segment length (mm) for OH/CH/AH; wavelength/UPR number for F; and 'H0' specifically for the convex hull (infinite radius).
rules.pass_condition: Nesting index values are physically consistent with Table C.2 and open/closed feature geometry (e.g., H0 for convex hull, positive UPR for closed roundness, positive mm for open straightness).
rules.fail_condition: Hull filter uses a non-zero number where convex hull H0 was intended, or an open-profile mm cutoff is confused with closed-profile UPR.
rules.remediation: Specify physically valid Table C.2 nesting indices matching the open or closed nature of the toleranced feature.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Normative Table D.1 Association Symbols (C, G, X, N, E, I) & Footnote a Restrictions
rules.audit_check: Normative Annex D (Table D.1) permits ONLY C (Minimax/Chebyshev), G (Least squares/Gaussian), X (Maximum inscribed), N (Minimum circumscribed), and constraint suffixes E (external to material) / I (internal to material) combining into CE, CI, GE, GI. Per Table D.1 Footnote a, X and N SHALL ONLY apply to spherical and cylindrical features for form (and features of size for datums).
rules.pass_condition: All reference association modifiers in compartment 8 (or ISO 1101 FC:) are valid Table D.1 codes obeying Footnote a.
rules.fail_condition: Invalid letter combinations (e.g., 'XE', 'NI', 'M', 'LS') appear in compartment 8, or X/N is applied to a flat plane or cone.
rules.remediation: Use only normative Table D.1 symbols (C, CE, CI, G, GE, GI, X, N) and restrict X/N to cylinders and spheres for form.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Normative Table D.2 Parameter Symbols (P, V, T, Q)
rules.audit_check: Normative Annex D (Table D.2) permits ONLY P (reference-to-peak), V (reference-to-valley), T (peak-to-valley total range — default), and Q (root mean square / RMS) in compartment 9.
rules.pass_condition: All parameter modifiers in compartment 9 are strictly P, V, T, or Q (with P and V paired only with C or G).
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard statistical codes (e.g., 'RMS', 'MAX', 'Ra', 'Rz', 'STD') appear inside compartment 9 of a geometrical tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Replace non-standard parameter text with exact Table D.2 symbols (P, V, T, or Q).

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Band-Pass Filter Cutoff Ordering (Long-Wave First; Higher UPR First for Closed Profiles)
rules.audit_check: Per Annex E.2 and 8.2.2.2.1, in a band-pass filter 'a-b', the long-wave pass cutoff ALWAYS comes first: for OPEN features (mm), smaller wavelength precedes larger wavelength (e.g., 'G0,8-2,5' passes waves >=0,8 mm and <=2,5 mm); for CLOSED features (UPR), HIGHER UPR precedes LOWER UPR (e.g., 'G50-15' or 'F50-15' passes undulations <=50 UPR and >=15 UPR).
rules.pass_condition: Open band-pass filters satisfy a < b (mm), and closed band-pass filters satisfy a > b (UPR).
rules.fail_condition: Band-pass cutoffs are inverted (e.g., 'G2,5-0,8' on a straightness profile or 'G15-50' on a roundness profile), creating an impossible/empty passband.
rules.remediation: Correct band-pass ordering so long-wave pass precedes short-wave pass (smaller mm first for open features; larger UPR first for closed features).

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Normative Graphical Proportions per ISO 81714-1 and ISO 3098-5
rules.audit_check: Per Normative Annex F, the sizes and graphical proportions of all Table 2 symbols and Figures F.1–F.5 auxiliary indicators SHALL harmonize with drawing lettering in accordance with ISO 81714-1 and ISO 3098-5 (frame height = 2h, symbol height proportioned to text height h).
rules.pass_condition: Tolerance indicators and auxiliary boxes have uniform harmonized heights and line weights matching drawing text.
rules.fail_condition: Auxiliary indicators are scaled inconsistently relative to the tolerance indicator frame or drawn with malformed proportions.
rules.remediation: Resize tolerance and auxiliary indicator symbols to uniform ISO 81714-1 / Annex F proportions.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Auxiliary Indicators SHALL Touch Tolerance Indicator (or Preceding Plane Indicator) With Zero Gap
rules.audit_check: Per Normative Annex F Notes (Figures F.1, F.2, F.3, and F.4), the leftmost point of every Intersection Plane, Orientation Plane, Collection Plane, and Direction Feature indicator SHALL physically TOUCH the right edge of the tolerance indicator (or the preceding auxiliary plane indicator) with ZERO visual gap.
rules.pass_condition: Every auxiliary plane/feature indicator abuts the right side of the tolerance indicator (or preceding auxiliary indicator) with zero gap.
rules.fail_condition: A visible white space gap separates an Intersection Plane, Orientation Plane, Direction Feature, or Collection Plane indicator from the tolerance indicator.
rules.remediation: Snap the leftmost vertex/edge of each auxiliary indicator directly against the right edge of the tolerance indicator or preceding auxiliary indicator.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: Normative Proportions and Narrow Line Width (dn) of the 'Between' (↔) Symbol
rules.audit_check: Per Normative Annex F Figure F.5, the 'between' symbol (↔) SHALL be drawn as a horizontal double-headed arrow using narrow line width dn proportioned to the adjacent capital letters (e.g., A↔B).
rules.pass_condition: 'Between' symbol renders clearly as a properly proportioned double-headed arrow (↔) between the two boundary letters.
rules.fail_condition: 'Between' is replaced with a hyphen ('A-B', ambiguous with common datum!), a single arrow ('A→B', retired!), or prose ('A TO B').
rules.remediation: Use the normative double-headed '↔' symbol (Fig. F.5) between the two boundary letters.

rules.section: Annexes C, D (Normative), E, F (Normative), and G: Filters, Form Elements, Symbol Proportions, and GPS Matrix
rules.title: ISO 1101:2017 General GPS Scope (Chain Links A, B, C) & Complementary Standards
rules.audit_check: Per Annex G (Table G.1), ISO 1101:2017 is a General GPS standard influencing chain links A, B, and C for Form, Orientation, Location, and Run-out. Specialized rules for datums (ISO 5459), patterns (ISO 5458), MMR/LMR (ISO 2692), linear sizes/envelope (ISO 14405-1), non-rigid parts (ISO 10579), edges (ISO 13715), and general tolerances (ISO 2768 / ISO 22081) are governed by their respective complementary ISO GPS standards.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing properly harmonizes ISO 1101:2017 geometrical indications with complementary ISO GPS standards (e.g., citing ISO 8015 / ISO 22081 or ISO 2768-mK without contradiction).
rules.fail_condition: Drawing mixes ASME Y14.5 rules (e.g., Rule #1 envelope default or RFS/MMC composite frames) with ISO 1101:2017 syntax on the same sheet.
rules.remediation: Ensure the entire drawing consistently adheres to the ISO GPS matrix (ISO 8015 + ISO 1101:2017 + complementary ISO standards) without mixing ASME conventions.
